items.title: Pay disputed 'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' collection claim
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.
items.computation: The letter gives an explicit calendar date rather than only a period: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026' (also framed as '72 Stunden' from the letter date 03.08.2026, which lands on the same day). 06.08.2026 is a Thursday, not a Saturday, Sunday or NW public holiday, so no §193 BGB shift applies. The printed date is therefore taken as the due date.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a debt-collection scam: it demands payment to a private-sounding foreign account (Lithuanian IBAN, account holder 'A. Petrauskas') that matches neither the sender (EuroClaim) nor the alleged original creditor (Lotto-Muster-Club Services) — never pay this account.

A genuine Inkasso company cannot itself order a 'Kontopfändung' (account seizure); this requires a German court judgment/Vollstreckungstitel obtained via a court, so this threat is legally false and is a pressure tactic typical of scam letters.

The claim 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos und verursacht weitere Kosten' is false and manipulative — a debtor always has the right to dispute a claim in writing, and doing so does not by itself create extra costs; this looks like an attempt to talk the recipient out of exercising legitimate rights.

The underlying claim stems from an alleged telephone-concluded 'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement', a well-known scam/pressure-sales pattern in Germany (dubious lottery/game clubs signing people up by phone); such contracts are frequently invalid or contestable.

The extremely short deadline ('72 Stunden') combined with threats of SCHUFA entry and criminal charges (Eingehungsbetrug) for a relatively small consumer debt is a classic high-pressure scam tactic and should be treated with suspicion; verify independently (e.g. with a consumer protection agency, Verbraucherzentrale) before any payment or reaction.

No court title, no original contract copy, and no verifiable German business address are provided — before doing anything, the recipient should check whether such a subscription/contract genuinely exists and consider not paying while seeking advice from a Verbraucherzentrale.
